title: Quiz: collections
description: Five questions on arrays, dictionaries, sets and tuples.

questions.question: What is ["a", "b", "c"][1]?
questions.why: Indexes start at zero, so index 1 is the second item.

questions.question: What does a dictionary lookup like ages["Zoe"] give you?

answers.text: 0 if there is no such key
Zoe's age, or a crash if there is none
An optional: Zoe's age, or nil if there is no such key

questions.why: The key might not exist, so the result is optional. Use ?? fallback or default: to supply a value.

questions.question: You need to check quickly whether a username is already taken, among millions. Which collection fits best?
questions.why: contains on a set stays fast however big it gets, and usernames are unique anyway.

questions.question: What is the difference between sort() and sorted()?

answers.text: sorted() changes the array itself; sort() returns a sorted copy
sort() changes the array itself; sorted() returns a sorted copy

questions.why: Swift's naming pattern: a plain verb changes the value, the -ed form returns a new one.

questions.question: Which is the best fit for a function that returns a minimum and a maximum together?

answers.text: A tuple like (min: Int, max: Int)

questions.why: Tuples group a few related values for a short time, with names for each part.
